stem: Which section title provides the most defensible primary anchor for associated-anomaly thinking?
explanation: Congenital Malformations is the correct answer because it is the most direct and defensible section title to anchor associated-anomaly thinking.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Congenital Malformations

optionExplanations.A: Correct because this section title directly relates to congenital anomalies and is the best primary anchor for associated-anomaly thinking.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because hereditary spherocytosis is a red cell disorder and not a congenital malformations section title.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because vomiting is a symptom topic and does not provide an anomaly-focused anchor.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because vasculitis is a inflammatory/rheumatology topic and not the best section title for congenital anomaly framing.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the pGALS musculoskeletal screen is a clinical screening tool, not a congenital malformations anchor.
